requirements.requirement: W1 — the MODIFIED 'A row is one line tall' drops 'no instrument output may add a line to the footer'
requirements.evidence: Reproduced by reading both texts. Living :208-211 states the rule twice: 'whatever an instrument returns, its cell MUST keep one line … so the footer's height is the number of declared rows' and the trailing clause. The delta (:22-26) keeps the first statement, adds 'each declared row adds one line to the footer' and 'any vertical space … MUST come from the footer's stack, never from a row's or a cell's line', and keeps the scenario 'Content that would span more than one line → the footer's height is unchanged'. An instrument output that added a line would make its row two lines, which the delta forbids. The clause is restated once, not dropped; the proposal announces it (:92-94: 'a row stays one line; any space between rows is the footer's stack's, never a row's or a cell's line'). Restoring the clause would put one fact in two places and push the paragraph (measured 465) past Joel's 500. Disposition: REJECT as a defect; no trim, no split, no change to the delta or the proposal.
